summary: Raimon Panikkar (1918–2010) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Barcelona, Complutense, Bonn, Mysore, BHU, and Lateran universities. He taught at Harvard (~1966–1971) and UC Santa Barbara (~1987–2010), where he became professor emeritus.

Raimond Gaita (born 1946) is a philosopher who studied at St Patrick's College, Melbourne High School, the University of Melbourne, and the University of Leeds. He held academic posts at King's College London (~1989–2011) and Australian Catholic University (~1999–2011).

Rajan Gurukkal (born 1948) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Calicut and held posts as Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (~1996–2008) and at IISc Bengaluru (~2010–2015).

Rajendra Chandra Hazra (1904–1982) was an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under Sushil Kumar De. He held posts at Jagannath University (1931), the University of Dhaka (1939–1949), and Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).

Rajendralal Mitra (1824–1891) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Hindu School and the University of Calcutta, and served as president of the Asiatic Society (~1885–1886).

Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay (1885–1930) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, and later held posts at Calcutta (~1908–1911), Presidency University, and Banaras Hindu University (~1928–1930).

Ralf Kramer (born 1971) is a Tibetologist. He studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and at the University of London, and served as Aris Librarian for Tibetan & Himalayan Studies at Bodleian Libraries (~2003).

Ralph Abraham (1936–2024) worked in philosophy and other fields, studying at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata SenSharma. He held posts at UC Berkeley (~1960–1962), Columbia University (~1962–1964), and UC Santa Cruz (attested 2009).

Ralph Lilley Turner (1888–1983) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After studying at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1907–1913), he held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1920–1922) and served as Director of SOAS University of London (~1937–1957).

Ralph T. H. Griffith (1826–1906) was an Indologist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, under Horace Hayman Wilson (~1845–1849). He succeeded James R. Ballantyne and served as Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1883).

Ram Karan Sharma (1927–2018) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Patna University and earned his PhD at UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau, later holding posts at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University and the Central Sanskrit Board.
Ram Mohan Roy (1772–1833) was a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He founded Presidency University, Kolkata in 1816 and also founded the Brahmo Samaj.

Ram Niwas Pandey is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under Hit Narayan Jha and studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and Pt. Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology.

Ram Shankar Tripathi (1929–2019) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held professorial posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1977–1994) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1989–1998).

Ram Sharan Sharma (1919–2011) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at Patna College, Patna University, and SOAS, later holding posts at Patna College (~1946–1970), SOAS, the University of Toronto (~1965–1966), and the University of Delhi (~1973–1985).
Rama Nath Sharma (born 1939) is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held professorships at the University of Rochester (~1968–1976) and the University of Hawaii (~1976–2012).

Ramaprasad Chanda (1873–1942) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Dhaka College and Scottish Church College, later holding posts at Rajshahi Collegiate School, University of Calcutta, and as Archaeological Superintendent at the Indian Museum (1921–1931).
Ramaranjan Mukherji (1928–2010) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1944–1953) and later held an academic post there (~1956–1970).
Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Vidyapith and at L. D. Arts College (attested 1938).

Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar (1909–2001) was an Indologist who studied at Mumbai and Heidelberg. He held posts at Fergusson College (~1932–1950), Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1949–1974), and served as Secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1939–1993).
